summary.text: 53-year-old man with subungual melanoma of the thumb metastatic to liver and lungs; combined CTLA-4 and PD-1 inhibitor immunotherapy was started in February 2019 and the authors report no other known ICI-DM risk factors beyond gender and regimen.

After two treatment cycles he developed rapid weight loss, polyuria and polydipsia over two weeks; capillary glucose was 757 mg/dL with glucosuria and metabolic acidosis, and he was admitted to Endocrinology. Blood glucose was 470 mg/dL, glycated hemoglobin 8.1%, islet cell, GAD and insulin autoantibodies were positive and C peptide undetectable, establishing ICI-DM.
He received hydration and intravenous and subcutaneous insulin, stabilised clinically over the next days, and was discharged on basal-bolus insulin; he continued ICI therapy with a complete response.

summary.text: 58-year-old woman with right-arm (deltoid) melanoma diagnosed October 2022 and treated surgically, with recurrence to left axillary lymph nodes at one-month follow-up, repeat surgery in November and combined anti-CTLA-4/anti-PD-1 immunotherapy from March 2023. She had pre-existing chronic autoimmune thyroiditis and primary hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 100 micrograms daily.

Two months after ICI initiation she developed grade 3 gastrointestinal toxicity (severe diarrhoea, dehydration) with temporary discontinuation; one week later she presented to the Emergency Department with refractory headache, photophobia and nausea. Head CT excluded stroke, infection and brain metastasis but raised suspicion of hypophysitis, MRI showed mild pituitary enlargement and the hormone panel (low cortisol and ACTH) was consistent with secondary adrenal insufficiency. High-dose glucocorticoids resolved symptoms, she was discharged on glucocorticoid replacement, and the team decided to resume ICI.

In September 2023 she presented with approximately 10 kg weight loss, polyuria and polydipsia; capillary glucose 314 mg/dL, blood glucose 450 mg/dL, HbA1c 8.2%, anti-GAD positivity only and undetectable C peptide confirmed ICI-DM. IV and subcutaneous insulin was started and she was discharged on a basal-bolus regimen.

The team then decided against continuing ICI therapy and opted for radiotherapy (delivery not explicitly described); a complete response was reported after fifteen weeks. In the Discussion the authors describe her response to ICIs as unsatisfactory, leading to the decision to switch therapy.

summary.text: 43-year-old man with clear cell renal carcinoma metastatic to the lungs diagnosed March 2024, treated with total nephrectomy in the same month and an anti-PD-1 agent from April 2024.

After eight cycles he developed autoimmune thyroiditis and primary hypothyroidism and levothyroxine was prescribed. After six more cycles a general practitioner found capillary glucose 455 mg/dL without symptoms suggestive of hyperglycemia; repeatedly high glucose led to referral. Admission fasting plasma glucose was 469 mg/dL with glucosuria and glycated hemoglobin 10.4%, TSH 52 uIU/mL, normal cortisol and ACTH, undetectable C peptide and a negative autoantibody panel.
Insulin therapy led to glycemic improvement over the following days and discharge on a basal bolus regimen; he is alive and continuing anti-PD-1 therapy.
